text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — Retail partner announced a 6h flash event next Wed 18:00-00:00 UTC. They expect a ~3.5x lift vs baseline. We need a concise capacity hedge plan (GPU hours, pre-warm, fallbacks).

Priya: Sounds tight. Do we have a forecasted RPS and token mix for their traffic? Any affinity to embeddings/long-form?

Sam: Baseline observed from pilot: 650 req/s steady. Expected peak ~2300 req/s during top hour. Median request ~120 tokens, tails to 1k tokens on product descriptions. Mix: 85% text gen (chat-style), 10% embeddings, 5% rerank.

Marcus: Quick calc: for model rdx-13b-q4 (quantized 4-bit) on H100-80GB we see ~85 tokens/s per GPU for the median workload with batching. For peak 2300 req/s and median 120 tokens -> roughly 276k tokens/s -> ~3250 GPU-seconds/s? math sucks, hold on.

Marcus: Recalc in simple terms: tokens/sec at peak = 2300 * 120 = 276k t/s. If one H100 sustains ~85 t/s (realistic with our runtime + batching), needed GPUs = 276k / 85 ≈ 3247 GPUs (obvious overestimation because batching across requests improves throughput). But with continuous-batching and prefix cache we can target 20x effective throughput improvement for similar prompts => practical need ~160-200 GPUs.

Lena: Important: that 20x cache/batch uplift only applies if we pre-warm prefixes and the product descriptions overlap. We should model two scenarios: 1) warm/cached (optimistic), 2) cold/unstructured queries (pessimistic).

Priya: Cost tradeoff: Reserved Dedicated capacity monthly cost >> burst on-demand credits for a 6h window. Recommendation: reserve 40% of expected peak (for SLA-critical routes) and rely on on-demand pool + soft-fallback routing for remainder. That keeps committed cost down.

Carlos: For the on-demand part, we should pre-assign region buckets. Primary: us-west / eu-west split by user geo. If eu-west has capacity constraints we failover to us-west with reduced-precision model (rdx-13b-q4 -> rdx-6b-q8) to save GPUs and egress.

Sam: Agreed. Also add network constraint: egress quotas from eu-west to partner CDN may spike. Action: coordinate with NetEng to raise inter-region egress cap for that 6h window and enable Traffic Shaping rule to prefer local region pools. @Oncall please ping NetEng. :rotating_light:

Oncall: Pinged NetEng, ticket 12345 created. They estimated 2-3h turnaround to raise soft caps; recommend notification by EOD today to avoid delays.

Marcus: Quick autoscaler config draft (for canary):
```yaml
policy: bucketed
buckets:
  - name: reserved
    target_gpus: 80  # 40% reserve
    min_instances: 10
  - name: ondemand
    scale_factor: 2.0
    max_instances: 500
prewarm: true
prewarm_profiles:
  - route:/api/generate
    top_prefixes: 200
```

Lena: We should also bake a routing rule to downgrade to rdx-6b-q8 when latency > 1.2s P95 or when gpu-queue-depth > 1000. Fallback preserves availability.

Priya: Simulation plan: run synthetic traffic with seq length distribution (70% 80-150 tokens, 20% 200-500, 10% >500) across 3 regions over 24h window to catch cold-cache path. Target: 95% of runs show P95 latency < 1.5s and cost delta within budget. Who can run the sim?

Carlos: I can schedule a sim on Friday. Need the job spec + model container (rdx-13b-q4 + rdx-6b-q8). Marcus can you provide container tags and perf profile table?

Marcus: Will push perf matrix to the runbook and attach container tags by EOD. Also adding KV cache warm-up script to the repo: //tools/cache_warm.sh — it accepts a CSV of top prompts.

Sam: Final ops checklist (short):
- [Priya] Approve reserve 40% capacity and cost cap ✅
- [Marcus] Perf matrix + containers (EOD)
- [Carlos] Sim job + results (Fri)
- [Lena] Routing + fallback rules merged (PR)
- [Oncall] NetEng egress ticket follow-up (in flight)

Priya: I'll run cost sim after Marcus uploads numbers. If pessimistic scenario requires >300 GPUs for >2h, we'll ask Sales to negotiate partner traffic smoothing.

Sam: Thanks team — let's keep thread for updates only. If any blocker, call standup 1h. :thumbsup:
